Apple's open-source Darwin kernel (XNU, xnu-8796.121.2) on Android phones with a Qualcomm SoC , the way Android is Linux on phones: a boot loader of its own, drivers of its own, a configuration system and a version of its own. The same kernel runs in QEMU with nothing of Apple's and nothing of any phone's ( make qemu-open ).
Documentation: docs/ , also on the project's website ( hakios-web ). Start with Getting started , Port a device or the Architecture .
Every part, as each device's own device.conf records it: Devices . The rows about the lock screen and the apps describe what happens when you add layer 2 below yourself.
The open core : the kernel port, the loader, the drivers, the tools. All source, in these repositories.
What you put on top : the kernel can start a user space that you supply. It was built so that it can start the Darwin userland 16.5 user space, which you lay out yourself from files you download from Apple; nothing of it is shipped, and nothing is circumvented to get it. Whether you may do that, and whether you want to, is your decision.
Apple's services (activation, Apple ID, iCloud, the App Store): not supported and not a goal.
By default the loader goes into RAM through fastboot boot , the system lives in RAM for a session, and a reboot brings the phone back to its own Android. The one thing written by default is the loader's own log (a few KB) to the logdump partition; with ufs_write=1 the kernel writes only to a partition darwin that you create yourself. This is a research bench, not a ROM.
Darwin in QEMU (Linux, 12 GB of disk, Apple's IPSW downloaded for you), and a session on the phone: QEMU , On the phone .
Repositories: common, SoC, device, UEFI
devices/manifest.conf in the common repository names each one and the revision it is at; tools/hakios-device.py sync clones them into devices/ and uefi/ . One repository per device: it carries its SoC's layer, and tools/hakios-device.py new makes one. How the repositories fit .
A device of your own is a repository over the common one: tools/hakios-device.py new makes it from the phone's own device tree, with every phone driver left out until it is ported. Each driver is an option of the kernel's own configuration ( CONFIG_HAKIOS_* , XNU's options and conf/files ), so a device's defconfig builds exactly the drivers it has. Port a device , Drivers in the configuration .
What is in the repository, and what never is
In it: only our own code and data: the patch to Apple's open-source XNU ( xnu/hakios.patch , APSL 2.0) and our files, the boot loader, our programs and libraries, the tools, prebuilt/ (built from this source; the loader without any Apple data: make loader makes the one that starts Darwin, on your machine, from your own IPSW), and the device and SoC directories.
Never in it: any file of Darwin (you build the system image on your machine from an IPSW you get yourself and hand to sysimage/unpack.sh ; nothing is downloaded for you, decrypted or circumvented); the phone's firmware (pulled from your own phone into fw-*/ , which git ignores); keys, certificates, activation, or anything that would make the phone pass as an iPhone to Apple.
Independent, and Apple-free at the core
HakiOS is an independent research project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple ; "Darwin", "iPhone", "XNU" and "Apple" are named only to describe what the code works with. The core kernel, the boot loader and the open tools build and run with nothing of Apple's:
No IPSW, no Darwin user space, no firmware. Booting the stock Darwin user space ( make qemu , make phone ) is an optional path that needs the IPSW and the phone's firmware, which you supply from your own device.
My code is under the license of the files it changes: the XNU patch under the Apple Public Source License 2.0 (Apple publishes XNU under it; the terms are met: changes are published as source, notices are kept), the rest as the file headers say. Darwin, its images, Apple's trademarks and the phone's firmware belong to their owners, are not in this repository and are not distributed by me; everyone takes them from their own phone and their own IPSW. "Darwin", "iPhone" and "Apple" are named only to describe what the code works with. If you believe a file here infringes anyone's rights, open an issue and I will remove it.
The detail is in separate files: LEGAL.md (what is and is not distributed, and the limits of these statements), COMPLIANCE.md (how the APSL 2.0 and other terms are met, and the items still to verify), THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md (every third-party component with origin and license), and NOTICE (the short canonical list). None of this is legal advice.
hakios is an experimental project focused on bringing darwin to android hardware. our goal is to make hakios free and accessible to everyone.
